title: CST by default, linked Monaco editors, comment translation, nested grammars, machine dialects and language versions
body:
## Summary

Fixes #14

This PR addresses issue 14 and the requirements of earlier issues and pull requests that had not been delivered. Every change is made in both JavaScript and Rust, and the two command lines print byte-identical output. The full case study is in [`docs/case-studies/issue-14/`](https://github.com/link-foundation/universal-translator/tree/issue-14-213b02ae6953/docs/case-studies/issue-14):

- `README.md`: timeline, the issue's requirements R1–R24, root causes and alternatives;
- `previous-requirements.md`: every earlier requirement with its status;
- `prior-art.md` and `architecture.md`;
- `requirements.lino`: CI fails while any requirement is neither done nor reported as blocked with a reason.

### Issue 14 requirements

- **A concrete syntax tree (CST) by default.** Whitespace and blank lines now survive a translation. The layout pass (`js/src/translation/layout.js`, `rust/src/layout.rs`) aligns the tokens of the output with those of the source and returns a `lineMap`. `--layout target` restores the emitter's own formatting.
  - `main`: `console.log( "Hello World!");` → `console.log("Hello World!");`
  - this branch: `console.log( "Hello World!");` → `console.log( "Hello World!");`
- **Monaco by default, with linked editors.**
  - Folding regions now work for every language.
  - Folding, selection, the cursor and scrolling are shared by both editors. Scrolling is mapped block by block, so blocks of different sizes stay aligned.
  - Lines that map to each other get matching colours, as in Compiler Explorer.
- **Comment and identifier language selectors on both sides.** The option checkboxes are now below the editors.
- **Comments are translated.** A shared multilingual vocabulary (`data/natural/vocabulary.lino`) is used both to detect a comment's language and to translate it.
  - `// Привет мир` → `// Hello world`.
  - «Привет» is now detected as Russian.
  - «Как хорошо покакать?» translates to "How good to poop?" (free prose translation).
- **Deeper grammars.**
  - Prose reads as `Prose > Sentence > Word`, with concepts and parts of speech.
  - Comments and strings are read with their own grammars (code in prose, prose in code). Long texts are stored once and referred to by id. Use `--shallow` for the plain tree.
- **A more general meta language.** `print` is a call to the library function `print-line`.
- **Assembly and intermediate languages.** NASM, GNU as, ARM64, LLVM IR, WebAssembly text, CIL and JVM bytecode are written and read back.
- **Language versions.** `javascript@es5`, `php@5`, `csharp@5`, `python@2`, `python@3.5`, `lua@5.1`, `java@1.4`, `swift@1` and `scala@2.9` are available. `registerLanguageVersion` adds a version of your own.
- **More tasks and corpora.**
  - 22 Rosetta Code tasks go through all 33 programming languages and the 7 machine targets.
  - 33 of the 34 programs of the Hello World Collection are read.
  - `check-equivalence` checks that a translation does what its source does.
- **Debugging and research.**
  - `--trace` prints the tree after every stage, and the web app logs translations and editor-sync events with `?debug`.
  - formal-ai was tried on six tasks; its failures are reported as link-assistant/formal-ai#1641 and link-assistant/formal-ai#1642.

### Screenshots

Line mapping in the linked Monaco editors:

![mapping](https://github.com/link-foundation/universal-translator/blob/issue-14-213b02ae6953/docs/case-studies/issue-14/screenshots/app-mapping.png?raw=true)

Comment and identifier language selectors on both sides:

![selectors](https://github.com/link-foundation/universal-translator/blob/issue-14-213b02ae6953/docs/case-studies/issue-14/screenshots/app-selectors.png?raw=true)

![style](https://github.com/link-foundation/universal-translator/blob/issue-14-213b02ae6953/docs/case-studies/issue-14/screenshots/app-style.png?raw=true)

### Tests

- JavaScript: `npm test` passes 1823 tests, with 1 skipped (shellcheck is not on the PATH locally).
  - Tests touched by this PR include `layout`, `comments`, `prose`, `nesting`, `language-versions`, `machine-dialects`, `hello-world-dialects`, `identifiers` and `ranking`. The web app has unit tests and end-to-end tests.
  - `npm run lint` and `node scripts/check-requirements.mjs` pass.
- Rust: every JavaScript test above has a twin under `rust/tests/` (for example `layout.rs`, `prose.rs`, `nesting.rs`, `language_versions.rs` and `hello_world_dialects.rs`).
  - `cargo clippy --all-targets -D warnings` and `cargo fmt` pass.
  - The full `cargo test` runs in CI.

### Still open or blocked

These items are tracked in `docs/case-studies/issue-14/previous-requirements.md` ("Concise list: everything still open"). None of them is claimed as done.

1. **Blocked:**
   - The Objective-C program of the Hello World Collection is Portable Object Compiler code that clang rejects.
   - Publishing the unscoped npm name `universal-translator` needs the owner's npm account. `npm view universal-translator version` gives `E404`.
   - The JavaScript CLI loads Meta Language from an environment variable until link-foundation/meta-language#230 is released.
   - The upstream process fix link-assistant/hive-mind#3929 is still open.
   - `Example app` on `main` needs `RELEASE_PR_TOKEN`; it passes on this PR.
2. **Partial:**
   - Rosetta Code: 22 tasks, not the whole set. Strings, higher-order functions, data structures, input/output, objects and concurrency are not covered.
   - Language versions: 8 of the 33 programming languages have versions (Python, JavaScript, PHP, C#, Lua, Java, Swift and Scala), and British English is the only natural variant.
   - TIOBE top 50: 22 languages are missing.
   - Classes of objects are not read.
   - Sentences have no phrase or clause structure.
   - There is no binary reader.
   - Library code is not translated.
   - Ranking frequencies are Zipf priors, not counted from a corpus.

title: Polish the web demo, Links Notation by default, plainer meta view, working skins (issue 12)
body:
## Summary

Fixes #12

This PR covers every point of issue 12: the web demo, the meta-language view, rules and settings stored as Links Notation instead of JSON, skins, a case study, debug output, upstream reports, and an audit of earlier issues. The JavaScript and Rust versions behave the same.

The case study (data, timeline, requirements, root causes, solutions, audit) is in [`docs/case-studies/issue-12/README.md`](https://github.com/link-foundation/universal-translator/blob/issue-12-6c3cea9725cc/docs/case-studies/issue-12/README.md).

## Requirements → implementation → verification

| # | Requirement | Done in | Checked by |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Content of any size; the title and inputs don't jump | `styles.css`: fixed control heights, pickers of fixed width, the example note on its own line of fixed height, panes between `--pane-min` and `--pane-max` | E2E `keepsTheLayoutStill`: the title and pickers stay at the same position for a 1-line and a 30-line text |
| 2 | Optional Monaco editor, highlighted from our meta language | `CodeEditor.js`, `monaco.js`, `highlight.js`; a "Text editor" setting (plain or Monaco). Monaco loads only when chosen | E2E `editsInMonaco`; `js/tests/universal-app-issue-12.test.js` |
| 3 | Left and right panes always the same height | `.pane` grid rows stretch to the same height; Monaco reports its content height | E2E `keepsTheLayoutStill`, `editsInMonaco` |
| 4 | "How it works" moved down | `App.js`: a full-width `about-panel` below the translator | Screenshots |
| 5 | Word wrap on/off | `#word-wrap` switch plus a setting; Monaco `wordWrap` | E2E `wrapsLongLines` |
| 6 | Rules on their own tab | Rules tab (`RulesEditor.js`, with rows and the Links Notation text); the Translate tab shows a note while rules are active | E2E `detectsAndTranslatesPartially`, `editsRulesAsLinksNotation` |
| 7 | Every element aligned | One control height, one corner radius, labels on one baseline, a square swap button, an options row that wraps on narrow screens | Screenshots (desktop, mobile, dark, glass) |
| 8 | No JSON by default; indented Links Notation instead | Rules: `readRules`/`formatRules` (JS) and `read_rules`/`format_rules` (Rust); the CLIs' `--rules` and the server accept `.lino`; the demo stores rules, standards, word standards and settings as Links Notation, and still reads JSON saved earlier. `coverage`/`detect` print Links Notation in both CLIs, and `--json` prints JSON | `js/tests/rules-notation.test.js`, Rust tests, `js/tests/issue-8.test.js`, `rust/tests/issue_8.rs`, E2E (the localStorage value starts with `output:`) |
| 9 | Meta language: `x:` only for unique keys; no `body: block` | `formatMeta` in `js/src/meta/notation.js` and `rust/src/meta/notation.rs`: one line per node, children nested under it, no `block`/`statements` lines, `otherwise` before the second branch; `--json` keeps the full structure | `js/tests/meta-notation.test.js`, `rust/tests/grammar.rs`, `rust/tests/issue_12.rs`, `experiments/issue-12-meta-parity.sh` (JS and Rust print the same for all 13 example programs) |
| 10 | Whole codebase and earlier issues/PRs double-checked | Audit of issues 1, 6 and 8 (see below) | Case study, "Audit Of Earlier Issues" |
| 11 | Skins didn't work | The app palette now applies only to the app skin; panel radius, opacity and blur come from the theme tokens; Monaco takes the skin colours; theme files are bundled so the desktop (`file://`) build works | E2E `changesTheSettings` (glass changes the panel in light and dark); `experiments/issue-12-skin-specificity.mjs` |
| 12 | Case study in `docs/case-studies/issue-12` | Issue data, before-screenshots, layout-shift measurements, timeline, root causes, alternatives considered (CodeMirror, Shiki/Prism/Tree-sitter, cascade layers…) | — |
| 13 | Debug output | Demo: `?debug` (or localStorage `universal-translator.debug=1`); the CLIs already have `--trace` | Manual |
| 14 | Upstream reports with repro, workaround and suggested fix | link-foundation/ui#292 (Vite can't bundle `readThemeFile`'s template-literal URL), link-foundation/ui#293 (compiled theme CSS loses to a host's dark palette) | Both open upstream; this repo works around both |
| 15 | Apply everything across the codebase, JS and Rust alike | Meta view, rules, and `coverage`/`detect` output are identical in both CLIs | Parity scripts and tests in both |

## Audit of earlier issues (1, 6, 8)

Fixed here:
- **B1**: the JS CLI crashed in shell pipes. When standard input isn't ready yet, `readFileSync(0)` throws `EAGAIN` (for example `(sleep 1; echo 'print(1)') | universal-translator translate python javascript -`), and a reader that closes early (`| head`) caused an unhandled `EPIPE`. Now `readStandardInput` waits through `EAGAIN`, and `EPIPE` ends the CLI quietly. The test `js/tests/cli-pipes.test.js` uses real shell pipes; it fails before the fix and passes after.
- **P9**: `coverage` and `detect` printed JSON by default, against requirement 8. They now print indented Links Notation in both CLIs; `--json` still prints JSON.

Not done in this PR. These are known gaps in translation coverage or the Rust port, each a separate task of the kind issue 8 tracks; the case study lists each with evidence:
- B2: the meta language has integers only, so `7 / 2` becomes `Math.trunc`.
- B3: `translate-program` needs the Meta Language 1.0 module.
- P1: some natural-language wordings aren't read.
- P2: comments are translated word by word.
- P3: the concrete syntax tree doesn't keep whitespace inside expressions.
- P4: few language versions.
- P5: no Wikidata words in Rust.
- P6: no ranking step.
- P7: Rosetta Code coverage is 39.4% of lines.
- P10: the Rust CLI has no `serve`.
- P12: no Hello World Collection corpus.
- JavaScript arrow functions and classes aren't read.

title: CI/CD without false positives, false negatives, warnings or errors: example app on main, strict lint, ShellCheck, CodeQL and npm audit gates, desktop skins on file://
body:
## Summary

Fixes #10

Each CI/CD workflow was checked for errors, false positives (red without a real problem), false negatives (green while something is broken) and warnings. Every one found is fixed in this pull request. The full case study is in [`dev/log/issues/10/pulls/11/README.md`](https://github.com/link-foundation/universal-translator/blob/issue-10-ac0b270fdd45/dev/log/issues/10/pulls/11/README.md). It has the requirements table, a timeline, root causes, the template comparison, the raw CI logs (`ci-logs/`) and before/after evidence (`evidence/`).

## Errors (red runs)

| Problem | Root cause | Fix |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `Example app` failed on every push to `main` (run 45623028339) | `scripts/update-preview-images.mjs` waited for `#calculator-title`, an id from the template's calculator. The translator renders `#translator-title`. The job only ran on `main`. | Wait for selectors the app renders (a test checks they exist). A read-only `preview-check` job renders the images on pull requests. Container steps use `bash`. Preview images regenerated. (6b3b57e, 2a1bb83) |
| Versioning dry run failed any pull request without a changeset, and the lint steps after it never ran | `@changesets/cli` 3 exits 1 with "No unreleased changesets found" | Skip with a notice when nothing is pending (6897d89) |
| The offline dry run failed with `ENOTCACHED` | `use-m` fetched `command-stream` from a CDN while `npm_config_offline=true` | Release helpers are exact devDependencies loaded from the lockfile (738132c) |
| The new CodeQL gate failed every run | Alert #5 was dismissed in code scanning, and the SARIF file does not record dismissals | `.github/codeql/accepted-findings.json` matches the rule, path and `primaryLocationLineHash` exactly, needs an alert URL and a reason, and fails when an entry is stale. Rejected findings print `path:line`. (ca695ee, 9e800cf) |
| `finds nothing in the tracked scripts and hooks` failed on Node, Bun and Deno (run 45649688140) | The job pins ShellCheck 0.11, but the test runs the runner's ShellCheck 0.9, which reports SC2015 for `[ ] && echo \|\| true` | The trace helpers use an `if` statement, which both versions accept (e4364a2, 0ba9e7c) |
| Deno failed `rejects a syntax error in js/tests/nested/check.test.js` on every run since the fixture was added (runs 45646051898 to 45652861265) | The Deno leg ran the gate on the runner's preinstalled Node. On Node 20 and 22, `node --check` exits 0 for an untyped `.js` file that uses `export`, even with a syntax error; Node 24 reports it. The repository supports Node 20 and later, so the gate itself had a false negative | Untyped `.js` files are checked through stdin as CommonJS, then as an ES module (822375b). Every test leg pins Node 24, as the template does (ce6ea41). The fixture also fails on git errors (727f3bf) |
| CodeQL `Analyze` failed at "Uploading results" (run 45649687987) | A transient GitHub outage; no analysis exists for that commit | No code change; the next run uploads normally |

## False negatives (green while broken)

- Lint warnings were filtered to changed lines and never failed. Now any warning fails (13780da), and the eight hidden warnings are fixed (c60ff67).
- `cargo doc` never ran (two broken intra-doc links), and Cargo's own warnings passed Clippy (f96e27f).
- The syntax gate checked only `scripts/*.mjs`, not `js/` (9cf89c5). On Node 20 and 22 it also passed untyped `.js` files with ESM syntax errors (822375b).
- Change detection skipped every check for shell scripts, Dockerfiles, CSS and similar files (cfa3ab1).
- Shell scripts called by workflows were never linted. They now go through ShellCheck (fb74d84).
- `npm audit --audit-level=high` passed moderate advisories in silence. There is now a full advisory report and a live deprecation check (26ab768).
- CodeQL uploaded alerts but never failed the run, and it skipped `examples/` (09789a0).
- **Desktop app skins were broken on `file://`.** Vite only warned that `node:fs/promises` was externalized, and every skin failed in Electron with `readFile is not a function`. Theme files are now bundled. A new `file://` e2e reproduces the problem, and any Vite warning fails the build (4aab2bf).

## False positives

- The status gate compared fork pull requests with `refs/heads/<branch>` instead of `refs/pull/N/head` (150e131).
- The budget wrapper could kill a command up to 1 s before its budget ended (1088b33).
- The common library translations step had a smaller budget than its shorter sibling, so its 70% warning fired on ordinary slow runners (e674adc).

## Warnings removed

- Node 20 deprecation and DEP0040/DEP0169 from `actions/cache@v4`: moved to v6 (f367b67).
- Deprecated secretlint preset (f367b67).
- Deprecated ESLint 9: moved to ESLint 10 (c60ff67).
- `npm warn deprecated glob@7/inflight/boolean/rimraf@2` in the example app (2a65e53).
- Line-limit warnings for `parser.js` (1498 lines) and `release.yml` (1425 lines) (908917b, 3b015c9).
- Vite chunk-size and externalized-module warnings (4aab2bf).
- Native translation budget warning (e674adc).
- `actions/checkout` and `actions/setup-node` moved to v7, as the templates use (f58ba7e).
- Dependency Review warned that `npm/human-signals` (through `command-stream` and `execa`) has an OpenSSF Scorecard of 2.8, below the default 3. Scorecards are still listed in the summary, but a low one no longer warns, as in the template (ac9e65c).

## Template best practices and upstream reports

The parts the [JS pipeline template](https://github.com/link-foundation/js-ai-driven-development-pipeline-template) already did better were ported:

- changed-files lint scope;
- `HEAD_REF` in the status gate;
- the budget wrapper (identical except the `trace` helper, which avoids SC2015 on the runner's ShellCheck 0.9);
- the ShellCheck job;
- the npm audit report;
- the CodeQL result gate;
- lockfile-loaded release helpers;
- the example app overrides;
- Node 24 pinned in every test leg;
- the Dependency Review scorecard settings.

Three problems also exist in the template and are reported there with a reproduction, workaround and fix:

- link-foundation/js-ai-driven-development-pipeline-template#319: the CodeQL gate fails forever on a dismissed alert, and its failures do not name a location.
- link-foundation/js-ai-driven-development-pipeline-template#320: the dry run fails when no changeset is pending.
- link-foundation/js-ai-driven-development-pipeline-template#321: the syntax gate passes untyped `.js` files with ESM syntax errors on Node 20 and 22.

A code search found these steps only in the JS template, so the other language templates are not affected.

## How to reproduce and verify

- Preview selectors: `js/tests/universal-app.test.js` ("waits for preview selectors that the app renders") checks that every selector the preview script waits for exists in the app source. Before the fix the script timed out on `#calculator-title` (`ci-logs/example-app-45623028339.log`).
- Desktop skins: `npm run build` in `examples/universal-app`, then `node examples/universal-app/e2e/file-protocol.e2e.mjs examples/universal-app/dist/index.html`. This fails before 4aab2bf (`evidence/file-protocol-e2e-before.log`).
- Dry run: `npx changeset version` in a clean checkout with no changeset gives `exit=1`.
- CodeQL gate: `js/tests/codeql-results.test.js` covers accepted, stale, edited-line and rejected findings.
- Syntax gate: `js/tests/javascript-syntax.test.js`. With the old gate and Node 22 first on `PATH`, `deno test -A js/tests/javascript-syntax.test.js` fails with "Expected 0 to be 1", as in CI. `experiments/issue-10/node-check-untyped-esm.sh` shows the Node behaviour.
- Budget wrapper and timeouts: `js/tests/ci-timeouts.test.js` and `js/tests/run-with-budget-warning.test.js`.

Debug output is off by default: `DEBUG=1` prints release script stack traces, `BUDGET_VERBOSE=1` and `PIPELINE_STATUS_VERBOSE=1` trace the budget wrapper and the status gate, `VITE_ALLOW_WARNINGS=true` lets a local Vite build finish despite warnings, and `CHROMIUM_EXECUTABLE` picks the browser for the `file://` e2e.

title: Better translation quality: comparison wordings, partial translation, detection, rules as data, Rosetta Code coverage
body:
## Summary

Fixes #8.

### Comparison wordings (the reported bug)

`Если n меньше или равно 1, сделать это:` and `больше или равно` now translate, along with the "obvious variations" in every natural language:

- Russian: `либо`, `не больше`, `<=`, `≤`.
- English: `at most`, `is less than or equal to`, and the symbols.

Python `pass` now reads as "do nothing".

Reproduce on `main`:

```bash
printf 'Если n меньше или равно 1, сделать это:\n  Ничего не делать\n' | npx universal-translator translate russian python
# main: error · this branch: if n <= 1:\n    pass
```

### Partial translation by default; all-or-nothing on request

- `translatePartial` translates what reads and keeps every unread part as a target-language comment with its error. For example, `// untranslated (line 2): …` is followed by the original line.
- `parsePartial` / the `coverage` command count the read lines and the missing parts.
- The CLI defaults to partial and has `--all-or-nothing`. The server takes `allOrNothing` and answers `{output, complete, errors, coverage, detected}`. The web demo has an "All or nothing" checkbox.

### Source language detection

`detectLanguage` scores each language as `100 × how much of the text its grammar reads`, plus evidence from the language's own syntax tables and templates. It needs no model or dependency.

- CLI: `translate auto <to>` and the `detect` command.
- Server: `from: "auto"`.
- Web demo: "Auto-detect" is the default source language.

### Rules as data at every stage

`createTranslator({ rules })`, `--rules file.json`, the server's `rules` and the web editor all accept the same JSON, with one list per stage:

- `source`: text before reading;
- `templates`: more wordings per natural-language template;
- `names`: a meta → meta renaming layer;
- `output`: text after writing.

Each rule can be plain text or a regex, and can be limited to one language. Rules are validated with clear errors.

### Visual rules editor

The web demo has a table per stage, a JSON import/export view, and a list of untranslated parts.

![Partial translation](https://github.com/link-foundation/universal-translator/blob/issue-8-a666e1cbe6e5/docs/screenshots/issue-8/partial-translation.png?raw=true)
![Rules editor](https://github.com/link-foundation/universal-translator/blob/issue-8-a666e1cbe6e5/docs/screenshots/issue-8/rules-editor.png?raw=true)

### Rosetta Code

`node scripts/rosetta-code.mjs all`:

- loads every programming and draft task (1772) through the MediaWiki API;
- keeps the solutions in our 32 languages in a git-ignored cache;
- sorts the tasks from the simplest meaning (median solution length, then how many languages solve it);
- reads them partially and writes a report of the missing lines and parts per task and per language.

The first full run reads **508,806 of 1,292,095 lines (39.4%)** over 1782 tasks ([report](docs/case-studies/issue-8/data/rosetta-code/README.md)).

The run also found a real bug. JS `Parser.next()` read past the end of the tokens, so the Ada reader looped forever on a cut text like `procedure P is`. It now throws "Unexpected end of program", as Rust already did, and a regression test covers it.

Translating *every* Rosetta Code solution is the issue's long-term goal, and this PR does not reach it. It adds the loading, ordering, partial mode and measurements the issue asks for, so the remaining ~60% of lines can be worked down task by task.

### Rust parity

The Rust crate and CLI get the same features:

- partial translation and `--all-or-nothing`;
- `auto` detection and the `detect` and `coverage` commands;
- `--rules`.

On the samples I compared, the Rust CLI's output matched the JS byte for byte. The Rust crate has no HTTP server, so the server changes are JS-only.

### Case study

[docs/case-studies/issue-8](docs/case-studies/issue-8/README.md) has:

- the issue data and a timeline;
- every requirement mapped to where it is done and how it is verified;
- the root causes, solutions and the libraries considered (Linguist, guesslang, highlight.js, franc/cld3, tree-sitter, ANTLR recovery, Blockly).

No upstream issue was needed: every root cause was in this repository.

## Tests

- `js/tests/issue-8.test.js`: wordings in every language, partial translation, CLI, coverage, detection, rules, server, and cut texts.
- `js/tests/rosetta-code.test.js`: offline fixture for extraction, sorting and counts.
- `rust/tests/issue_8.rs`: mirrors the JS tests.
- `examples/universal-app/e2e/translate.e2e.mjs`: auto-detect, the Russian example, partial output, a rule from the editor, and all-or-nothing.

## Security note

CodeQL flags `js/regex-injection` in `custom-rules.js`. Compiling the user's own pattern is the purpose of a `regex: true` rule, and on the command line the pattern comes from the user's own `--rules` file.

The HTTP server refuses regex rules by default, so remote clients cannot send ReDoS patterns. `createTranslationServer({ allowRegexRules: true })` opts in. Plain-text rules use no RegExp at all. Whether to dismiss the alert is left to the maintainers.

### CodeQL note
CodeQL alert #5 (`js/regex-injection` at `js/src/translation/custom-rules.js:46`) was dismissed as *won't fix*: building a `RegExp` from `find` is the requested regex-rule feature. The server refuses regex rules unless `allowRegexRules` is set, and plain rules never build a RegExp.

Fixes #6

## Summary

This PR builds on the issue 1 translator. It adds the meta language view, a language switch that does not fail, random examples, one entry per language with versions, semantic primes for every natural language, settings based on link-foundation/ui, concrete syntax trees by default, a separate comment language, a Standards editor, word standards of at most 1024 words with recursive Wikidata definitions, and a re-check of every issue 1 requirement.

The case study is in [`docs/case-studies/issue-6`](https://github.com/link-foundation/universal-translator/tree/issue-6-c597ff1041d9/docs/case-studies/issue-6). It has the issue data, research, existing libraries and the [requirements inventory](https://github.com/link-foundation/universal-translator/blob/issue-6-c597ff1041d9/docs/case-studies/issue-6/requirements.md). `requirements.lino` is checked in CI by `scripts/check-requirements.mjs`, together with the issue 1 and issue 8 inventories.

## Requirements

| Issue requirement | What was done | Verified by |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Meta language version of the left and right expressions | `formatMeta` (JS and Rust) writes the meta program as Links Notation. The demo has a "Show the meta language" switch | `meta-notation.test.js`, `rust/tests/grammar.rs`, e2e |
| Changing the left language does not fail | The right text is translated into the newly chosen left language | e2e |
| Buttons generate random examples | Program, Function, Statement (Sentence is removed). Each picks a random supported algorithm and two random languages | `examples.js`, e2e |
| Semantic primes for exactly all human languages | The 65 primes for every natural language in `data/natural/semantic-primes.lino`. Every language has a `minimal-<language>` version | Gate check `primes-everywhere`, natural goldens |

title: Universal translator: 32 programming languages (with Lean and Rocq), machine code, 30+ controlled natural languages, fragments, CLI/API/Docker and web demo
body:
Fixes #1

## Summary

This PR adds a translator for programs. It does not match templates: it reads source text with per-language grammar tables and rewrites it through rules. It translates between **32 programming languages** (including **Lean 4** and **Rocq**), **three machine targets** (NASM x86-64, CIL, JVM/Jasmin) and **controlled versions of 30+ natural languages**. The JavaScript (`js/`) and Rust (`rust/`) implementations write byte-identical output for every golden translation.

```text
source ──parser──▶ source tree ──understanding rules──▶ meta ──type inference──▶ typed meta
  ──meaning rules──▶ ──custom layers──▶ ──context rules──▶ ──emitter──▶ target text
  ──lowering──▶ stack machine ──▶ NASM / CIL / JVM (Jasmin)
NASM / CIL / JVM ──reader──▶ stack machine ──lifting──▶ meta
controlled natural text ──reader──▶ meta ──writer──▶ controlled natural text
```

### Requirements gate (test-driven)

`docs/case-studies/issue-1/requirements.lino` lists every requirement from the issue and its comments. `docs/case-studies/issue-1/rosetta-coverage.lino` lists the Rosetta Code algorithm types. `scripts/check-requirements.mjs` checks each requirement against the repository; for example, it compares the language lists of both implementations and checks that every task has a golden in every language. It fails CI (`Rust and cross-language translation` job, and `js/tests/requirements.test.js` under Node, Bun and Deno) unless every requirement is **done** or **blocked with a written reason**.

The gate caught real gaps during this work. The Rust implementation was missing 10 languages; that was fixed and the gate now passes.

### Web demo

![Web demo translating a Python function to Rust](https://github.com/link-foundation/universal-translator/blob/issue-1-35d65b774bf6/docs/screenshots/web-demo.png?raw=true)

`examples/universal-app` is a React demo in which any programming or natural language can be translated to any other. You can paste a whole program, one function or one statement. The `web-e2e` job in `.github/workflows/example-app.yml` drives it in Chromium (`examples/universal-app/e2e/translate.e2e.mjs`) and takes the screenshot above.

### Fragments: statements, functions or a whole program

`translateFragment` / `parseFragment` (JS) and `translate_fragment` / `parse_fragment` (Rust), plus `universal-translator translate --fragment`, accept a statement, one or more functions, or a whole program. Each comes back as the same kind of fragment in the target. A fragment only has to be complete: a function must end with its closing. Otherwise the translator fails with the reason and the line, for example `The fragment is not complete: it ends before its closing (line 2)`. Goldens for every language are in `examples/programs/fragments/translated/` and are checked by `write-fragments.mjs --check`.

### CLI, library, HTTP API and Docker

- `universal-translator serve` starts an HTTP API (`GET /languages`, `POST /translate`). It reads `--port`/`--host`, then `PORT`/`HOST`, then `.lenv`, through lino-arguments.
- `js/src/index.js` (with types) and the `rust/` crate are the libraries.
- The `Dockerfile` image runs the CLI and the server. The release workflow builds it and smoke tests the CLI and the HTTP API.

### Source layout and best practices

- Sources are split into `src/meta` (shared types and trees), `src/formal` (programming languages, Lean, Rocq and machine code) and `src/natural` (human languages, with a reader and a writer), in both `js/` and `rust/`. The `source-layout` check rejects imports that point outwards from the meta layer.
- [`docs/case-studies/issue-1/best-practices.md`](https://github.com/link-foundation/universal-translator/blob/issue-1-35d65b774bf6/docs/case-studies/issue-1/best-practices.md) maps the associative technology stack, the code architecture principles and all 17 CI/CD best practices to evidence, or gives a reason when one does not apply. `cargo clippy -D warnings` now runs in CI.
- **Test coverage is required by CI.** `npm run test:coverage` replaces `npm test` in the Node.js job. It fails below 94% line, 91% branch or 95% function coverage of `js/src` and `bin`; current coverage is 95.4%, 92.1% and 96.5%. The Rust crate runs the same goldens, but CI does not measure its coverage.

### Programming languages (32) and machine code

| | |
| --- | --- |
| Languages | JavaScript, TypeScript, Python, Ruby, Lua, PHP, C, C++, C#, Java, Go, Rust, Kotlin, Swift, Perl, Dart, Scala, Julia, R, Groovy, Objective-C, Nim, D, Pascal, Fortran, Ada, Visual Basic .NET, Bash, MATLAB/Octave, Zig, **Lean 4, Rocq** |
| Dialects | Pascal, Fortran, Ada, VB.NET, Bash, MATLAB/Octave and Zig have their own program layout. They are dialects of the shared parser and emitter (`js/src/formal/dialects/`, `rust/src/formal/dialects/`). Lean 4 programs use `partial def` and `IO`. Rocq programs are pure `Fixpoint`s over an output monad defined in a small runtime, and are evaluated with `Eval vm_compute`. |
| Machine targets | NASM, CIL and JVM are written through a named stack machine and read back by lifting, so machine code translates to every language and between targets. |
| Modes | context-dependent (default, adapts comments such as C "function call" → C# "method call"), literal, same-effect |
| Extensibility | Every stage and rule list is an option of `createGrammarTranslator`; custom meta → meta layers are supported. |
| Common library | `common-library/` (output operations only, one file per language), enabled with `--common-library` |

### Controlled natural languages

- Data lives in `data/natural/*.lino`; `js/src/natural/` and `rust/src/natural/` read and write the same texts byte for byte.
- Covers the 30 most spoken languages (English, Chinese, Hindi, Spanish, French, Arabic, Bengali, Portuguese, Russian, Urdu, Indonesian, German, Japanese, Marathi, Telugu, Turkish, Tamil, Vietnamese, Korean, Italian, Persian, Swahili, Tagalog, Thai, Polish, Ukrainian, Hausa, Gujarati, Punjabi, Dutch), each in a small controlled form (`cnl-default`).
- Profiles for the standards named in the issue:
  - ASD-STE100
  - Attempto Controlled English
  - Gellish (English and Dutch)
  - SBVR Structured English
  - Plain language (ISO 24495-1)
  - E-Prime
  - Basic English, VOA Special English and Globish
  - Minimal English, Minimal French and Minimal Polish, built on the **65 semantic primes** of NSM (`data/natural/semantic-primes.lino`)
- `checkText` and the `check-words` command enforce each standard's rules: sentence length, allowed first words, forbidden words such as "to be" in E-Prime or "shall" in plain language, vocabulary limits, and Gellish relation phrases.
- Translations run natural → meta → any programming or machine language, and back: `universal-translator translate russian python`, `translate python spanish`.
- Every example program is written in every natural language and profile under `examples/programs/natural/`. Each text is read back to the same meaning and checked against its standard.

### Rosetta Code and Hello World

18 tasks in `examples/programs/` are translated to all 32 languages, the 3 machine targets and every natural language, then run natively:

- hello world
- factorial
- greatest common divisor
- FizzBuzz
- sum of squares
- Fibonacci
- Ackermann
- Towers of Hanoi
- leap year
- sum of digits
- hailstone
- 99 bottles
- primality by trial division
- mutual recursion
- perfect numbers
- sieve of Eratosthenes
- bubble sort
- sum and product of an array

Algorithm types covered (from `rosetta-coverage.lino`): output, integer arithmetic, conditionals, iteration, functions, recursion (including mutual recursion), number theory, text concatenation, and **integer arrays** (new: array values in the meta language, all 32 languages, NASM/CIL/JVM and natural-language sentences).

**Blocked, with reasons recorded in `rosetta-coverage.lino`.** These are not presented as done. Rosetta Code has more than 1,300 tasks, and these types need values the meta language does not have yet:

| Type | Why it is blocked |
| --- | --- |
| floating-point | Machine targets and the meta language use 64-bit integers only |
| string manipulation | Text can be printed and concatenated, but not indexed or transformed |
| higher-order functions | Functions are top-level declarations only |
| data structures | Records, maps, stacks and queues need compound values |
| input/output | Programs only write to standard output, which is what the native checks compare |
| objects and concurrency | Not supported |

**Classes as fragments** are also **blocked** (`class-fragments` in the gate) for the same reason: the meta language has no objects or classes, so a class has no meaning to translate yet.

The gate reports `rosetta-algorithm-types` and `class-fragments` as **BLOCKED** with these reasons. Every other requirement is **DONE**.

## Verification

- **`npm test` (Node, Bun, Deno) and `cargo test`.** Every task is translated to every language, machine target and natural language and compared with the goldens in `examples/programs/translated` and `examples/programs/natural`.
- **`examples/programs/verify-native.mjs --require-all [--common-library]`.** The `native-translation` CI job compiles or runs each translation with its real toolchain and compares the output with the JavaScript original. The toolchains include Lean 4 (elan), Rocq (opam), fpc, gnat, gfortran, octave, zig, nim, ldc, Objective-C, Swift, Kotlin, Scala, .NET and Jasmin.
- **`experiments/verify-syntax-exchange.sh`.** The JS and Rust command lines list the same 32 languages and write identical output.
- **`node scripts/check-requirements.mjs`.** The requirements gate described above.
- **`npm run test:coverage`.** The coverage gate described above.
- **`web-e2e`.** The browser test of the demo.
- **`--trace`.** Logs each pipeline stage.

### CI reliability (native translation job)

- Toolchain archives are cached. Each download attempt is capped at 3 minutes and falls back to a mirror: Google's Maven Central mirror for Groovy and `zig.linus.dev` for Zig, all checked by SHA-256. This fixes a run where the step hung on a stalled download.
- `verify-native.mjs` runs its checks in parallel worker processes.
- `js/tests/ci-timeouts.test.js` keeps each job's step budgets within 70% of its backstop.
- Budgets are sized for slower runners. One run needed 330 s for all native translations and over 360 s for the common library translations, while a typical run needs about 220 s and 250 s. Every translation passed, but the 360 s budget ran out. The step budgets are now 540 s and 480 s, and the job backstop is 100 minutes so the budgets stay within 70% of it.

### CodeQL

- `js/incomplete-sanitization` flagged the Lean `s!"…"` brace escape, because it was chained after `escape()` where CodeQL cannot see that backslashes were already escaped. Brace escaping now happens inside `escape()` as the `escaped-braces` format. The output is unchanged, and a regression test in `js/tests/grammar.test.js` checks that `` `a\\b {c} ${name}` `` becomes `s!"a\\b \{c} {name}"`.
- CodeQL still lists an older alert on `docs/case-studies/issue-3/original-format-release-notes.mjs`. That file came with the initial commit and is not part of this PR, and the CodeQL check passes.

The data files use Links Notation (`.lino`). The PR contains exactly one changeset (`.changeset/sharp-programs-translate.md`). The case study is in `docs/case-studies/issue-1/`.

title: A tool to do translation between languages

type.name: Feature
type.description: A request, idea, or new functionality

body:
Hypothesis: translation in unrestricted grammars may be solved with dependent translation.

As we do in dependent logic in relative meta logic (when probability of single statement depends on probability of other statement, including recursively).

Translation changes depending on physical or abstract referent (or resolution of meaning of the word).

And sometimes multiple resolutions of meaning are intentional as in irony, paradoxes as so on.

All of paradoxes are links and fundamental laws, where we link something that is opposite or contradictory, but enviably connected.

So may there there is a way to deterministically translate between all languages, including natural languages.

We also need to make sure we precisely record any imprecision of any statement.

Like for example `person` is any person, `white person` is `any white person`, where `white` can reference anything white about that person, like `any person with a white skin` or `any person fully painted white` or `any person mostly white` and so on.

But as long as we make more concrete description the range of possible values gets smaller.

That means for example when we use associative model with type system defined as fractal like:
Type -> SubType
SubType -> SubType
SubType -> Value.

We actually still get type, subtype and value as types, but on each step we make them much more narrow.

So it looks like there should be one to one match between natural language and formal type system.

So we always work with ranges, and by calculating frequencies of language corpus we can have some probabilities which more specific type or description is most likely.

Yet for best translation (most likely and more correct) we should prefer such translation, which survives the round trip.

For example:

`белый` <-> `white`

`белый человек` <-> `white person`

In both languages these are highly likely.

And this example actually survives round trip, so that is the translation we should end up with using by default.

In programming language it may mean:

```
struct Person {
   Color color = Color.White;
}
```

And so on.

We also can see how Person is usually described on GitHub, and in the internet and so on, and if we have knowledge about corpus, we can have some probabilities on what to include.

We can also use the language description for requirements that will adjust requirements.

So when we define enough dependent details about anything in a language, we just specify a more concrete type, set or category.

That is the vision.
